title: Loop language: raw Lua
description: The Shape 1 loop written in Lua. Use this when the loop language lacks something; "Edit as Lua" in the Loop tab turns any loop script into Lua like this.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Rules every solver needs. The constant n is set in the Loop tab.
num(1..n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Solver A proposes candidates: here, any set of numbers.
{ pick(X) : num(X) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The atoms solver A and solver C share. glue(T) makes T an interface atom:
% its value in a candidate is fixed when the check runs.
glue(pick(X)) :- num(X).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: every glue(T) makes T an interface atom.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Solver C looks for a counterexample: a sum X + Y = Z inside the candidate.
1 { sum(X,Y) : num(X), num(Y), X <= Y, X + Y <= n } 1.
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(Y).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X+Y).
#show sum/2.

% relevant(T): the interface atoms the counterexample depends on.
% The refinement says: at least one of them must change.
relevant(pick(X)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(X+Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
fragments.description: Looks for a counterexample to a candidate (solver C) and marks the atoms it depends on with relevant/1.

loop.text:
-- A raw Lua loop: the text runs inside rt.run(function() ... end).
-- It is the Shape 1 script, compiled by hand. See the manual for the rt API.
local A = rt.solver("A", {"shared", "abstraction"}, {})
local C = rt.solver("C", {"shared", "check"}, {})
local G = rt.link("G", A, C, {"shared", "glue"}, {})
rt.prepare()                      -- grounds the solvers; call once, after the declarations

local found = 0
A:search{ on_candidate = function(M)
  local X = C:solve{ assume = G:of(M) }
  if X then
    M:reject(G:clause(M, X))
  else
    found = found + 1             -- not rejected: M is a solution
  end
end }
rt.log("solutions:", found)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
